        "stability": "Set random_state for reproducibility; still expect some jitter across umap-learn versions/BLAS. For epoch comparability use aligned/procrustes-aligned or parametric UMAP fixed encoder.",
        "failure_modes": "False neighbors in dense regions; torn clusters (one identity split across distant islands); distance distortion means 2-D neighbors ≠ embedding neighbors; cluster shape/size not trustworthy (distill.pub How to Use t-SNE Effectively; Understanding UMAP; UMAP arXiv 1802.03426; Nature Reviews Methods Primer 2024)."
      },
      "runtime_cpu": {
        "scale_10k_100k": "umap-learn on 10k×128-D: typically seconds–low minutes on modern multi-core CPU; 100k×128-D: minutes to tens of minutes depending on n_neighbors and n_epochs. Approximate nearest neighbors (pynndescent) dominate.",

        "notes": "CPU path is standard for umap-learn; GPU UMAP (cuML) not available on A1 ARM CPU."
      },
      "verdict": "HIGH VALUE for Workbench: directly addresses pain (a). Build as admin-only atlas (zoomable sprites, color by cluster_id, click→merge/split actions). Do NOT use 2-D coords as clustering or gate signals.",
      "evidence": []
    },
    "training_diag": {
      "use_case": "Per-epoch embedding drift/collapse viz for FIR-7 occlusion adapter",
      "beyond_obvious": [
        "Aligned UMAP: fit on epoch-0 (or concatenated) then project later epochs with same mapper / Procrustes align successive maps for comparable frames",
        "Parametric UMAP trained once mid-run for fixed coordinate system across epochs",
        "Complementary metrics (not projection-only): embedding norm stats, pairwise cosine hist, class/center collapse (intra vs inter identity cosine), linear CKA / SVCCA between epoch embeddings, silhouette on labeled Golden-150",
        "PaCMAP or densMAP as secondary views when UMAP tears clusters",
        "Trajectory plots of same identities across epochs in aligned 2-D"
      ],
      "verdict": "USEFUL as DIAGNOSTIC tier only; pair with quantitative collapse metrics. A1.Flex sufficient for post-epoch batch UMAP on validation embeddings.",
      "evidence": []
    },
    "active_curation": {
      "use_case": "Rank faces/clusters by uncertainty + 2-D outliers for human review queues",
      "approach": "Use embedding-space signals (cluster silhouette, nearest-centroid margin, soft-assignment entropy, density outliers) as primary ranking; 2-D UMAP for display/context only. Uncertainty-ordered queues accelerate Golden-150 and tenant curation.",
      "tools": [],

      "evidence": []
    },
    "library": {
      "name": "umap-learn",
      "license": "BSD-3-Clause (confirm on PyPI/GitHub)",
      "dependency_weight": "Moderate: numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, numba, pynndescent, llvmlite—numba/llvmlite are the heavy deps; fine on A1 if ARM wheels available",
      "never_as_gate": "CONFIRMED standard guidance: UMAP/t-SNE projections distort global distances; never use 2-D distances for clustering, identity gates, or automatic merge/split decisions. Use original high-D embeddings (pgvector cosine) for any automated signal; projection is human visualization only.",
      "evidence": []
    }
  },

  "q1_umap": {
    "atlas": {
      "use_case": "CLUSTER-CURATION ATLAS: project tenant or Golden-150 face embeddings (128-D) to 2-D UMAP, render zoomable sprite atlas of face thumbnails colored by cluster_id for human merge/split/outlier review",
      "verdict": "HIGH VALUE — directly attacks Workbench pain (a). Ship as admin-only atlas; wire click-through to merge/split actions. Never use 2-D coords as clustering or gate signals.",
      "best_practices": {
        "n_neighbors_range": "Docs default 15; sensible general range 5–50. For ~1e3–1e5 face points: start 15–30 (local identity neighborhoods). Raise toward 50–100 only if global structure must dominate. Very low (2–5) tears graphs into chains; very high loses fine merges/splits.",
        "min_dist_range": "Default 0.1; sensible 0.001–0.5. For identity islands/clumpy QA: 0.0–0.1. For readable Fashion-MNIST-style spread: ~0.1–0.3. Higher values (0.5–0.99) blur local topology.",
        "metric": "Use metric='cosine' for SFace-style L2-normalized face embeddings (matches pgvector cosine gate).",
        "densMAP": "Built into umap-learn via densmap=True; dens_lambda default 2.0 (raise to prioritize density, lower ~0.1 toward classical UMAP). Recommends n_neighbors≈30 for reliable local density. Helps when identity cluster sizes/densities vary (common in tenant data).",
        "parametric_UMAP": "umap.parametric_umap.ParametricUMAP (TensorFlow) learns a neural encoder → out-of-sample transform without full refit. Ideal for streaming new tenant faces and epoch-aligned training diagnostics. Tradeoff: slight fidelity loss vs classical UMAP; needs TF dep.",
        "supervised_UMAP": "Pass cluster labels as y= in fit for semi-supervised tightening. For QA atlas: prefer light supervision or post-hoc coloring only — heavy supervision can hide the true merges/splits operators need to find.",
        "stability": "Set random_state for bit-stable runs; random_state forces single-thread path (slower). Still expect small jitter across umap-learn/numba/BLAS versions. For atlas product: pin package versions + store projection coords in DB.",
        "failure_modes": [
          "Cluster sizes in 2-D mean nothing (density equalization)",
          "Inter-cluster distances often meaningless",
          "False neighbors / torn clusters (one identity split across islands)",
          "Low n_neighbors invents structure from noise",
          "2-D distance ≠ high-D cosine distance — never gate on projection"
        ]
      },
      "runtime_cpu": {
        "scale_10k": "Typically tens of seconds on modern multi-core CPU for ~128-D after numba warmup",
        "scale_70k_mnist_ref": "CONFIRMED: MNIST 70k×784 embeds in ~42–60s; Fashion-MNIST ~49s on 3.1 GHz i7 (umap-learn docs). densMAP MNIST wall ~2min20s vs UMAP ~1min43s on same machine.",
        "scale_100k": "Order of a few minutes on multi-core CPU (pynndescent kNN dominates); expect ~2–10 min on A1.Flex 4 OCPU depending on n_neighbors",
        "a1_flex_enough": "YES for batch atlas of 10k–100k 128-D vectors (4 OCPU/24GB). Golden-150 is trivial. Full large-tenant 1e5 nightly batch OK; interactive full-refit of huge tenants: prefer subsample + parametric UMAP or incremental transform.",
        "notes": "A1 is ARM — verify numba/llvmlite aarch64 wheels. No cuML GPU UMAP on A1. M1 laptop can orchestrate but keep heavy fits on A1."
      },
      "evidence": [
        {"url": "https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/parameters.html", "grade": "CONFIRMED", "claim": "n_neighbors default 15 (range demos 2–200); min_dist default 0.1 (demos 0.0–0.99); local vs global tradeoff documented"},
        {"url": "https://pypi.org/project/umap-learn/", "grade": "CONFIRMED", "claim": "n_neighbors often 5–50 (default 10–15 sensible); min_dist 0.001–0.5 (default 0.1); densMAP dens_lambda=2.0; Parametric UMAP via tensorflow; MNIST 70k under a minute; Fashion-MNIST 49s; license BSD-3"},
        {"url": "https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/densmap_demo.html", "grade": "CONFIRMED", "claim": "densmap=True; densMAP slower but relatively constant overhead; dens_lambda controls density priority"},
        {"url": "https://distill.pub/2016/misread-tsne/", "grade": "CONFIRMED", "claim": "Cluster sizes mean nothing; inter-cluster distances often meaningless; hyperparameters and early stopping create false structure; multi-run instability"},
        {"url": "https://pair-code.github.io/understanding-umap/", "grade": "CONFIRMED", "claim": "Interactive UMAP n_neighbors/min_dist guidance; MNIST 70k in <3 min vs t-SNE 45 min"},
        {"url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03426", "grade": "CONFIRMED", "claim": "UMAP paper: fuzzy topological manifold model; theoretical basis for parameters"},
        {"url": "https://doi.org/10.1038/s43586-024-00363-x", "grade": "CONFIRMED", "claim": "Nature Reviews Methods Primers 2024 (Healy & McInnes): how to apply/interpret UMAP; cites as community primer"},
        {"url": "https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-00801-7", "grade": "CONFIRMED", "claim": "densMAP paper (Nature Biotechnology 2021) — density-preserving UMAP variant"}
      ]
    },

atlas.use_case: CLUSTER-CURATION ATLAS: project tenant or Golden-150 face embeddings (128-D) to 2-D UMAP, render zoomable sprite atlas of face thumbnails colored by cluster_id for human merge/split/outlier review
atlas.verdict: HIGH VALUE — directly attacks Workbench pain (a). Ship as admin-only atlas; wire click-through to merge/split actions. Never use 2-D coords as clustering or gate signals.

best_practices.n_neighbors_range: Docs default 15; sensible general range 5–50. For ~1e3–1e5 face points: start 15–30 (local identity neighborhoods). Raise toward 50–100 only if global structure must dominate. Very low (2–5) tears graphs into chains; very high loses fine merges/splits.
best_practices.min_dist_range: Default 0.1; sensible 0.001–0.5. For identity islands/clumpy QA: 0.0–0.1. For readable Fashion-MNIST-style spread: ~0.1–0.3. Higher values (0.5–0.99) blur local topology.
best_practices.metric: Use metric='cosine' for SFace-style L2-normalized face embeddings (matches pgvector cosine gate).
best_practices.densMAP: Built into umap-learn via densmap=True; dens_lambda default 2.0 (raise to prioritize density, lower ~0.1 toward classical UMAP). Recommends n_neighbors≈30 for reliable local density. Helps when identity cluster sizes/densities vary (common in tenant data).
best_practices.parametric_UMAP: umap.parametric_umap.ParametricUMAP (TensorFlow) learns a neural encoder → out-of-sample transform without full refit. Ideal for streaming new tenant faces and epoch-aligned training diagnostics. Tradeoff: slight fidelity loss vs classical UMAP; needs TF dep.
best_practices.supervised_UMAP: Pass cluster labels as y= in fit for semi-supervised tightening. For QA atlas: prefer light supervision or post-hoc coloring only — heavy supervision can hide the true merges/splits operators need to find.
best_practices.stability: Set random_state for bit-stable runs; random_state forces single-thread path (slower). Still expect small jitter across umap-learn/numba/BLAS versions. For atlas product: pin package versions + store projection coords in DB.
failure_modes: Cluster sizes in 2-D mean nothing (density equalization)
False neighbors / torn clusters (one identity split across islands)
Low n_neighbors invents structure from noise
2-D distance ≠ high-D cosine distance — never gate on projection

library.name: umap-learn
library.dependency_weight: Moderate: numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, numba, pynndescent, tqdm, llvmlite. Heavy bits are numba/llvmlite (compile/JIT). Optional: matplotlib/datashader/holoviews for plot; tensorflow for parametric_umap; tbb for x86 speed. Package itself ~90KB wheel.
library.never_as_gate: CONFIRMED standard guidance: UMAP/t-SNE 2-D distances are distorted; cluster size/shape/separation in projection are not trustworthy metrics. NEVER use projection distance as clustering signal, identity gate, or automatic merge/split. All automated decisions must use original 128-D (or future 512-D) embeddings in pgvector (cosine). Projection is human visualization only. (Even umap-learn's 'using UMAP for clustering' path embeds then clusters in higher-D UMAP space carefully — not 2-D atlas coords.)

q2_dcface.summary: DCFace (CVPR 2023, arXiv 2304.07060) is a two-stage dual-condition diffusion generator: (1) unconditional DDPM G_id samples novel ID faces; (2) dual-condition mixer G_mix combines ID image X_id with style image X_sty via patch-wise style extractor + time-step-dependent ID loss. Operator-cleared synthetic identity generator for FIR retrain data.

artifacts.generator_checkpoints: pretrained_models/ from Google Drive folder (G_id DDPM on FFHQ, G_mix, style extractors, etc.) placed under dcface/
artifacts.code: https://github.com/mk-minchul/dcface — synthesis.py, stage1 unconditional generation, style bank align, train.sh
artifacts.download_links_doc: Dataset Drive folder + pretrained weights Drive folder linked in README

compute.paper_training_Gmix: 10 epochs, batch 256, AdamW lr 0.001 — 8 hours on 2× A100
compute.paper_sampling_500k: DDIM 200 intervals; generating 500K samples ≈ 20 hours on 1× A100 → ~0.144 s/image amortized at 200-step DDIM
compute.a10_24gb_feasible: YES for inference/synthesis. A10 24GB can run DDPM/DDIM face diffusion at batch≥1 (often batch 4–8 with fp16). Expect ~1.5–3× slower than A100 → rough 30–60 GPU-hr for 0.5M images, 70–140 GPU-hr for 1.2M at similar step counts. VRAM: 24GB sufficient for 112–256px class models if batch managed.
compute.cpu_only: NOT practical. Diffusion sampling is GPU-bound; CPU multi-hour-per-image class — reject for N×M production packs.
compute.oci_a10_burst_est: At ~$2/GPU-hr: 0.5M ≈ $60–120; 1.2M ≈ $140–280 (order-of-magnitude; depends on DDIM steps/batch). Prefer downloading released 0.5M/1.2M packs first unless custom style bank / occlusion-heavy styles needed.
compute.m1_laptop: Orchestration only — do not run DCFace inference on 8GB M1

config_knobs.identity_count_N: Number of unique X_id images from G_id (unconditional_sampling.py: --num_samples). Paper filtered 200k→~105k unique (r=0.3 cosine) then 62,570; FR packs use 10k or 20k IDs.
config_knobs.images_per_id_M: Styles sampled per ID from style bank (random or match gender/ethnicity). Ablation packs: 50 imgs/ID; oversample xid adds +5 copies of frontal X_id per label.
config_knobs.style_id_mixing: synthesis.py --id_images_root + --style_images_root; patch grid size (1×1…7×7, best FR at 5×5); style sampling random vs match; ID sampling random vs ethnicity-balanced; oversample_xid flag
config_knobs.diffusion_sampling: DDIM timestep_respacing / intervals (paper 200); diffusion_steps 1000 train; use_fp16; batch_size
config_knobs.losses: L_MSE + λ L_ID (time-dependent cosine interpolation between X_id and X_sty features)

A100 80GB PCIe ~$1.19–1.39/hr on-demand; A100 SXM ~$1.49/hr; H100 PCIe from ~$1.99/hr; Community Cloud spot often 40–60% below on-demand (interruptible).

adapter_scale.workload: FIR-7 PEFT: YuNet fine-tune (few M params) + SFace residual adapter 128→r→128 — hours not days

oci_a10.pros: Data local, env already known, stop instance after job

hf.est_cost_usd: A10G $1–1.5/hr → often cheaper list rate than OCI $2; A100 $2.5/hr comparable
hf.pros: Jobs/AutoTrain less ops if stack fits HF images; per-minute billing
hf.cons: Upload consented data to HF; env pinning for custom YuNet/SFace may fight platform images; AutoTrain not built for this stack; H100 removed from Spaces

adapter_scale.recommendation: Prefer OCI A10 burst for adapter-scale: privacy for any consented samples, zero data movement, cost ~$10–25/run. Use HF Jobs A10G only if pure-synthetic and you want managed job API — list rate can undercut $2 but ops+privacy usually lose.

campaign_scale.workload: Future retrain: SCRFD-arch detector + AdaFace-style 512-D embedder on ~0.5–1.2M synthetic (days on single A100-class)

oci_a10.est: A10 ≈0.5–0.7× A100 throughput for CNN FR training → multi-day to 1–2 weeks wall for full campaign
oci_a10.pros: Data local (DCFace packs on OCI), no egress, full control of multi-stage detector+embedder pipeline
oci_a10.cons: Slower than A100/H100; single-GPU unless more burst capacity added

hf.est: A100 $2.50/hr or H200 $5/hr Jobs — faster wall-clock; 48–120 A100-hr → $120–300
hf.pros: Faster GPUs on demand; multi-GPU configs if budget allows
hf.cons: Upload 0.5–1.2M images; checkpoint persistence across Jobs needs Hub or re-upload; custom SCRFD/AdaFace training loops = Jobs Docker not AutoTrain; consented mix still privacy-sensitive

campaign_scale.spot_alt: RunPod A100 spot ~$0.7–1.2/hr effective can beat both if checkpoint-resilient — worth evaluating for pure synthetic campaign, not for production PII pipelines.
campaign_scale.recommendation: Campaign-scale pure synthetic: OCI A10 is acceptable and simplest (data already local); if wall-clock matters, burst to RunPod/Lambda A100 (~$1.2–2.0/hr) with checkpoints, or HF Jobs A100 at $2.50. Avoid HF for any consented real faces. Do not use Spaces for multi-day trains (sleep/billing footguns).

q3_econ.recommendation: Adapter-scale (FIR-7): OCI A10 burst only. Campaign-scale (SCRFD+AdaFace on DCFace 0.5–1.2M): default OCI A10 if days OK; else rent A100 (RunPod spot or Lambda on-demand) with synthetic data only — HF Jobs A100 as third choice when you want managed API and accept Hub data residency. Keep UMAP/curation on A1.Flex CPU. Never put consented face datasets on HF or Nomic cloud.

structuredOutput.summary_for_decision: Q1: Ship a Workbench CLUSTER-CURATION ATLAS with umap-learn (BSD-3, cosine metric, n_neighbors 15–30, min_dist 0.05–0.1, random_state pinned); optional densMAP for density; Parametric UMAP for new points + epoch-aligned FIR-7 diagnostics. A1.Flex CPU is enough for 10k–100k. Rank curation queues on high-D uncertainty (pgvector), not 2-D. Prefer FiftyOne (Apache-2.0) + Embedding Atlas (MIT) self-hosted; projections must NEVER gate merge/identity. Q2: DCFace is cleared and practical — use released 0.5M/1.2M packs first (FR: LFW 98.6%, avg ~89.6@0.5M / 91.2@1.2M). Custom gen needs GPU (paper 500k≈20 A100-hr); A10 24GB OK, CPU not. BOVIFOCR fork adds env pins, rec tooling, similarity QA — use for ops. Q3: Adapter FIR-7 on OCI A10 (~$2/hr, data local). Campaign retrain: OCI A10 default for synthetic; else RunPod/Lambda A100 if speed needed. HF A10G is list-cheaper than your A10 but worse for privacy/ops on custom FR stacks — avoid for consented data.
